newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: U.N., OAU pledge reconstruction aid to Kabila.
newsitem.headline: U.N., OAU pledge reconstruction aid to Kabila.

text.p: The United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity will help Laurent Kabila reconstruct his renamed Democratic Republic of Congo, a U.N. special envoy said on Friday.

Mohammed Sahnoun, U.N. special envoy to Central Africa, said Africa should realise former Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko's government collapsed because it was "clearly unpopular" and had run down the country, potentially one of the continent's richest.

"The United Nations and the OAU will do everything in their power to assist the Democratic Republic of Congo mobilise international efforts in its reconstruction programme and urge all multilateral and bilateral donors to make their contribution to its development," he said at a closed-door OAU foreign ministers meeting. Reuters obtained a copy of the speech.

The ministers are meeting in Harare to prepare an agenda for a three-day OAU summit in the Zimbabwean capital from June 2. It was Sahoun's first conference with African leaders since Kabila's rebels drove out Mobutu earlier this month.

"We have to admit that the outgoing regime was clearly unpopular and that there was little opposition to the...swift progression in the country," he said of Kabila's seven-month campaign against Mobutu, Zaire's leader for 32 years.
Sahoun who represented both the U.N. and the OAU in mediation efforts in the former Zaire, said the organisations had helped Africa's third largest country avoid more bloodshed.

"The UN/OAU Peace Plan was an important leverage in the process. It enabled us to maintain dialogue between all sides while allowing the African and international communities to increase pressure on all concerned to avoid total confrontation and bloodshed," he said.
Mobutu fled Kinshasa ahead of a rebel advance on the capital, paving the way for a largely peaceful takeover by Kabila.

Next Monday's OAU summit is expected to draw some 40 heads of state and government, including Kabila, and is expected to discuss among other issues, the Great Lakes Region, the coup in Sierra Leone and political developments in Somalia and Angola.
OAU officials said it would also focus on Africa's quest to establish a common market in the next century.
